description: All instances are the word "need" (or its plural "needs") used as a noun referring to a requirement or necessity in various contexts.
All instances of "one" used as a determiner or number word, typically in phrases like "at least one" or "nearest one [unit]".
Instances of the relative pronoun "which" (and its capitalized form "Which") used to introduce relative clauses or questions.
Prepositions that introduce phrases indicating conformity, compliance, or relational positioning in formal or technical writing.
Last names or surnames of people mentioned in various contexts.
Legal terminology referring to parties in court proceedings, with some non-legal terms included
Instances of the modal verb "can" expressing ability, possibility, or permission in various contexts.
Technical terms describing problems, malfunctions, or issues in systems and software.
Research and legal terminology with broader professional contexts
Forms of the verb "have" (including "have," "has," "had," and "having") used as auxiliary or main verbs to express possession, experience, or obligation.
All instances are the noun "people" (and one "person") used as a general term referring to groups of individuals in various contexts.
Verb forms of "use" and "used" indicating utilization or employment of something.
French function words (articles, pronouns, conjunctions) preceded by a space token
All instances use "portion" as a noun referring to a part or section of something larger.
